The knight alternates square colors with every move, since each knight's move changes the sum of the row and column indices by an odd number. The lower-left square is dark, so after an odd number of moves (2009 is odd) the knight must stand on a light square. There are 32 light squares on the board.

Every light square is reachable in exactly 2009 moves. The knight's graph on the 8×8 board is connected and contains odd cycles, so once the move count is large enough, any square of the correct color can be reached in exactly that many moves. With 2009 moves, that condition holds, so all 32 light squares are possible.

Therefore the knight could end on 32 squares.

ANSWER: 32
